newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Blockade shuts Bangladesh's Chittagong port.
newsitem.headline: Blockade shuts Bangladesh's Chittagong port.

text.p: Cargo handling at Bangladesh's main Chittagong port was suspended on Tuesday as lorry drivers blockaded jetties to protest against the death of a transport worker, port officials said.
The worker, Abdul Wahab Noman, was killed when iron pipes rolled on him as he took a nap on one of the jetties on Monday night.

Angered by the port authority's alleged negligence in ensuring safety for port workers, the drivers parked their trucks on the road leading to the jetties. They are demanding compensation for Noman's family, the officials said.
The Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) has called for a meeting with leaders of hundreds of truck drivers later on Tuesday to try to end the wildcat strike.
M. Mohsin, CPA's Traffic Director, said the death of Noman was an accident. "The resultant wildcat action is unfortunate," he said.

There were 19 ships at the jetties and eight at the outer anchorage awaiting loading, unloading and berths on Tuesday. Over 100,000 tonnes of cargo and 11,861 containers were piled up at the port, the officials said.
